CHIEF COMPLAINT: Lower back pain for 1 week.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: 35-year-old presents with lower back pain that began after lifting a heavy box. Pain is dull, worse with bending, no radiation to legs.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY: No chronic conditions.

VITALS: BP 120/76, HR 70, Temp 98.2F, RR 14.

PHYSICAL EXAM: Lumbar paraspinal tenderness, no midline tenderness, straight leg raise negative bilaterally, normal gait.

ASSESSMENT: Acute lumbar strain.

PLAN: NSAIDs, heat, activity as tolerated, avoid heavy lifting for 2 weeks, follow up if no improvement.
